quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing at night to help other drivers see you. Bright colors and reflective materials make you more visible on the road.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Make sure other drivers can see you.
Keep other drivers guessing about what you will do.
Always ride very close to other vehicles.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers to reduce crash risk. Use your signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not work as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: What should you think about when choosing where to ride in your lane?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead of you.
Which part of the lane gets you there faster.
Whether you can pass more cars from that position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you and you have enough space around you. This helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Check if the seat is comfortable.
Assume it is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times.
Ride it like your own bike since most are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, get to know it. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes, and learn the gear pattern.

questions.question: What should you do with the laces on your shoes while riding?
questions.explanation: Always tuck in your shoelaces so they do not get caught on your motorcycle while riding.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Choose a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It explains how to operate and maintain your bike.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive an accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single most important thing you can do to protect yourself and reduce your risk of death or serious injury in an accident.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one drink, can you safely ride?

options.text: Yes, your skills will not be affected.
Yes, as long as you ride slowly.
No, alcohol may still affect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, alcohol may still affect you.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average, but this varies. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Effects from the alcohol may still remain.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Effects from the alcohol may still remain.
questions.explanation: On average, your body eliminates one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system. Your ability to ride and your judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: Riding gloves are often made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield provides the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, eye protection is not required if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: A good way to handle someone tailgating you is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass you. Speeding up only makes them tailgate you faster, which increases danger.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Lets the rider use engine braking.
Should not be done near other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets the rider use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through smooth downshifting is useful for motorcyclists. If you use engine braking, activate your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely so they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose part of your legs.

questions.explanation: Wear pants that cover your entire legs and are made of leather or sturdy synthetic material. Clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but loose enough to allow movement.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after having one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected by alcohol.
Effects from the alcohol may still remain.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Effects from the alcohol may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your system. This buildup can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly scan the road ahead for:
questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead to watch for changing traffic, hazardous road conditions, and possible escape routes. Be ready to react to any changes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road are slippery surfaces. Ride with extra caution on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are not important since motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.
Are very important to warn other drivers of your plans.
Should not be used if no vehicles are nearby.
Are more complicated than signals on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to warn other drivers of your plans.
questions.explanation: As a motorcyclist, you are vulnerable. Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do. Use them every time you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many accidents happen there. Motorcyclists and other drivers can easily collide at intersections.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots too small to be a problem.
Have blind spots you must check by turning your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots you must check by turning your head.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: For maximum protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: For maximum protection, use a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can improve visibility by:
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials. Also use your headlight at all times and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A properly maintained motorcycle will continue to ride like new. Regular maintenance checks should be part of your routine care.
